Details

Status for the 15 October talk. The question behind it: did the n_TOF set-up see what it was built to see, so that repeating it at LNL is realistic?

  1. What changed since Athens (slide 2) and what Geant4 said we should see (slide 3).
  2. Did we see the ²⁷Al pairs, and do they look like Al? (slides 4–8)
  3. X17 legs vs Al legs: penetration and what it does to two-track statistics (slides 9–11).
  4. Where the single tracks come from (slides 12–13).
  5. Calorimetry and MM dE/dx (slides 14–15). Verdict and LNL (slide 16).

Data: the is2_v2 re-pass at the capsule-focus k (stage3_is2_v2_cf, y up since 14 Oct), chambers A and C, tracks ≥ 12 ms after the flash, t0 ≤ 300 ns, |tan| < 0.6, production period (run_69 onward, the noisy-DREAM side of 23 July). Hover the dotted terms and the data points for values, counts and provenance.

Since Athens: one calibrated re-pass, cosmic truth, and Geant4 through the real reconstruction

the work between the Athens meeting (end of September) and 15 October

y now points up

14 Oct

Stage 3 had stored y mirrored since 7 Sep. Confirmed by the wiring, cosmic-muon timing (p = 4×10⁻¹¹) and the plastic PMT timing; every live stage-3 set regenerated. The source now sits on the capsule nose, where Geant4 puts it.

A calibrated re-pass (is2_v2)

9–12 Oct

In-situ cosmic calibration (drift velocity, kernel), the 3-strip seeder (+40–52 % confirmed tracks) and a two-sided slope search. Wall purity A 0.38 → 0.59, C 0.49 → 0.66; it drops junk pairs and keeps the real ones.

Beam-off cosmics as truth

2–8 Oct

41 runs, 57.6 h, put on the n_TOF clock. The A–C muon line calibrates the angle scale; the in-beam muons read it right to 1–4 %. The beam/cosmic wall gap is electron scattering, not the reconstruction.

Geant4 through the real reco

7–13 Oct

g4_digi injects Geant4 charge into real quiet triggers and runs the production reconstruction, so data and simulation are compared after the same losses.

Same-chamber pairs vs Geant4

12–13 Oct

Correlated pairs found (0.15 % of late events), shape compatible with Al e⁺e⁻, rate ⅛ of Geant4. The 12 Oct "vertex excess" was an early-time artefact and is retracted.

Calorimetry closed

8 Oct

Plastic scale fixed on muons; liquids threshold-limited; MM dE/dx and the soft-leg energy discriminant killed by their own criteria.

From ntof_athens_26/data/thermal_accounting/ (F1.csv–F5.csv, the Athens contract; MX17_Full_Geant/scripts/thermal_accounting.py, condor 4278922). Per neutron entering the capsule, E < 2 eV.

4

Details

Singles. Data tracks per trigger divided by Geant4 track-like singles in acceptance per trigger gives an effective efficiency 0.67 (A) / 0.52 (C). The digitised reconstruction of the same Geant4 events gives 0.54 / 0.45. The data/expectation ratio is the cover's ×1.25 / ×1.15.

Pairs. The prediction is the Geant4 ratio of events with two reconstructable leptons to events with one, times the measured P(2 tracks | 2 leptons) / P(≥ 1 | 1) from the digitised reconstruction, so the opening angle and the close-pair loss are in it. The brackets (other efficiency routes) span 0.12– 0.52.

Why the wall double ratio is not a test. P(both legs on the wall | pair) / P(one | single)² is ~0.55–0.6 for event-mixed (unrelated) pairs too.

Source tables: /media/dylan/data/x17/sept26_prelim/same_chamber/cmp_*.csv (same_chamber_compare.py).

There are correlated same-chamber pairs: 0.15 % of late events, the same in A and C

share of tracked events with a second same-chamber track, per ToF bin · fit a + b·rate over 12–75 ms

Before 12 ms the fraction is pile-up: it follows the rate.

After 12 ms the rate falls ×3.5 and the fraction flattens at 0.15 % (A) / 0.16 % (C). A part that does not scale with the rate is one particle source making two tracks.

That is ~2,051 (A) and ~1,660 (C) correlated pairs; accidentals are ~38% of all late pairs.

Geant4: 78% (A) / 75% (C) of reconstructable same-chamber pairs are one photon's e⁺e⁻.

is2_v2 re-pass, capsule-focus k · A and C, all runs from run_69 onward

5

Details

The method. Accidental pairs scale with the instantaneous rate, correlated ones do not. Fitting the fraction f(t) = a + b·rate(t) over 12–75 ms separates them without any event mixing or vertex test. χ²/ndf is 64/10 (A), so the statistical error is understated by ~2.5; the conclusion that a ≠ 0 holds at many σ.

Why not 0–12 ms. 77 % of chamber A's pairs fall there; they are flash and epithermal pile-up, and the capsule-pointing purity of tracks is 6–25 % there against ~45 % later. The beam's own captures peak at 5–6 ms, but the capsule tracks we record are 90 % after 12 ms (delayed neutrons). Details: same-chamber-pairs note, slides 2–3.

Code: same_chamber_compare.py → cmp_tof_fraction.csv, cmp_tof_fit.csv.

Details

Data. Late real same-chamber pairs minus the accidental share (from the rate fit, A 38 %) times the late event-mixed shape. Errors include the subtraction.

Models. Geant4 e⁺e⁻ = one photon's conversion pair; "all pairs" adds Compton + delta ray and the rest (75–78 % of it is e⁺e⁻ anyway); "unrelated" = event-mixed late tracks. Geant4 pairs are folded through the measured resolution, |tan| < 0.6 and the per-view two-track efficiency (same_chamber_g4.response), so the dip below ~10° is the close-pair loss, in both.

Reading. A: Geant4 e⁺e⁻ χ² 6.6/6, all pairs 2.5/6, unrelated 26.0/6. The difference comes mostly from the 0–10° and 40–50° bins, so it is a preference, not a separation; the Geant4 histogram has only ~60 weighted pairs per arm and its own error is in the χ². C does not discriminate (its Geant4 χ² is the worse one). Medians: data A 25°, Geant4 26°. A global y flip would not move any of this: opening angles are mirror-invariant.

7

Details

The direct route (same_chamber_compare.expectation, "digitised Geant4 through the reconstruction"): r₂ = Geant4 events with ≥ 2 leptons in the gap per event with ≥ 1, times P(2 tracks | 2 leptons) / P(≥ 1 | 1) measured on g4_digi (A 0.54, C 0.45 for one lepton). Because the digitised events carry Geant4's own opening angles and separations, the close-pair loss and the opening-angle distribution are in the prediction, as they were in that reconstruction pass. Data/Geant4 = 0.13 (A), 0.12 (C).

The bracket routes use the measured per-view two-track efficiency of is2_v2 cf (two_track_efficiency_axis.csv) on Geant4's true separations; they give 0.12–0.52.

Next iteration. Getting below 20 mm (T1's joint fit, off in this pass) would add up to ~45 % more pairs in both data and prediction. It raises the statistics; it does not by itself change the ratio. Re-digitising with is2_v2 is the step that fixes the prediction's reconstruction, and it should be done before the next comparison.

Scattering on the way out, not the reconstruction, breaks the Al pair vertex

Geant4 truth, 13,545 conversion leptons from the 10⁹-neutron nose campaign · p·β·θ = 0.40 MeV·rad at every energy

Geant4 neutrons_thermal_trig_2cm_nose (nose-first capsule, centred beam), same_arm_pairs.py truth per lepton

8

Details

What is measured. For each conversion lepton that crosses ≥ 20 mm of a drift gap: the line through its first gap step along its gap direction, and that line's distance of closest approach to the true conversion point. The deflection is the angle between the vertex→gap chord and the gap direction. No reconstruction is involved.

The law. The median p·β·θ is 0.40 MeV·rad in every bin from 0.5 to 6 MeV (0.31 at 6–9 MeV, n = 92), which is multiple scattering: θ ∝ 1/(pβ). The path is the capsule wall (0.6 mm Al barrel, up to 5.5 mm at the nose, 0.9 mm CFRP), then about 23 cm of air and the drift cathode. The median conversion lepton has 2.1 MeV at the gap, so it arrives 9° off its birth direction.

X17 legs (8–10 MeV) are scaled with the same law: 2.3–2.9°, miss 9–11 mm, comparable to the angular resolution (~7 mm). 90%–82% of X17 legs pass within 20 mm of their vertex, against 31% of Al legs.

Details

Curves (leg_penetration.c2_ladder): the calorimetry C2 Geant4 guns (e⁻ and e⁺ averaged, from the capsule centre at θ 90°, aimed at a plastic bar, 20k per energy, production geometry), conditional on the lepton reaching the drift gap. The stack behind each chamber: 3 mm SiPM wall, 20 mm plastic, ~18 mm liquid (LAB).

Spectra. Al: conversion leptons from ²⁷Al(n,γ) in the capsule vessel that cross ≥ 20 mm of a gap, Geant4 10⁹-neutron campaign; their gap-entry energy + 0.6 MeV (half the measured upstream loss of a pair) to put it at the capsule. X17: both legs of X17 → e⁺e⁻ pairs (pair sim, 10⁷ events) whose legs enter two different arms.

Numbers folded with the curves (energy only: the lepton is aimed at the stack): plastic > 0.3 MeV — X17 88%, Al 28%; plastic ≥ 2.5 MeV — X17 82%, Al 11%; liquid — X17 57%, Al 2.6%.

With the real geometry (each lepton's own Geant4 deposits, so the gaps between bars and the bar size count): plastic ≥ 2.5 MeV — X17 26%, Al 3.8%; liquid — X17 24%, Al ≈ 2.0% (Al liquid estimated from the curve). The ratio X17/Al is ×7 at the trigger level and ×10–20 at the liquid in both views.

Caveat for X17. At wide opening angles (≥ 140°) the soft X17 leg has only 3.9–4.8 MeV and about half of those stop before the plastic (calorimetry note, slide c2). The hard leg always crosses.

An Al pair is recorded mostly because something else fired the trigger: a Compton electron from the same capture (76 % of trigger legs).

Its two tracks then rest on the Micromegas alone, with the scintillators unable to confirm either leg: a soft, close, same-chamber pair is the hardest two-track case.

75% of these pairs really are born within 20 mm of the axis. The test cannot see them because two lines at 25° cross far from where they were born once each has been bent by ~9°.

Geant4 truth, 1,772 same-chamber conversion pairs (A and C); X17 column from the scaled scattering law of the previous slide

11

Details

Why near-parallel lines are the problem. The intersection of two lines at opening angle α moves by about δ / sin α along the bisector when one line is displaced by δ. With δ ≈ 33 mm and α ≈ 25°, the midpoint lands ~78 mm away; Geant4 says 75 mm (median). Small angles are worst (0–15°: 1.6 %), and no bin passes more than 3 %.

The X17 case is different in all three factors. Its legs carry 4–5× the momentum, so the miss per leg is ~9 mm; they go to opposite chambers, so the vertex test is "does each line pass the axis" rather than "where do two near-parallel lines cross"; and the 470 mm A–C lever arm makes the line itself well defined. The 67–82 % assumes the same wall and air as the Al pairs (X17 is born in the gas and crosses the same wall) and ignores resolution, which adds ~7 mm in quadrature.

So the 2026-10-12 "vertex excess" could never have been the Al pairs: a test that real pairs pass 2 % of the time and chance passes 2–3 % of the time cannot show a ×2 excess of them. The late-only result (A ×1.00) is what Geant4 predicts.

Through-going cosmics and beam punch-through are a small, separate class: the A–C cosmic rate matches the muon flux, and in-beam "through-goers" rarely reach the liquid.

Geant4 neutrons_thermal_trig_2cm_nose · data: is2_v2 re-pass (cf), run_69 onward

12

Details

Geant4 split (leg_penetration.singles): every lepton that crosses ≥ 20 mm of the A or C drift gap in an event where some arm fired the emulated trigger. Pair leptons are 24% of single tracks — more than the 10 % of trigger legs, because a soft pair leg reaches the gap but not the plastic. The capture: almost all on the capsule's Al vessel, which is what the capsule-nose image (next slide) shows.

Data/expectation: data tracks per trigger / Geant4 singles per trigger = 0.67 (A), 0.52 (C), against the digitised-reconstruction efficiency 0.54 / 0.45.

Capsule purity: tracks whose line passes within 15 mm of the measured source, minus a shuffled-angle null, ≥ 20 ms (capsule_tof.py). Geant4's value comes from g4_digi through the same reconstruction.

What else is in the late data. Late triggers follow a 23.5 ms exponential (the hall's neutron die-away, not the beam's own captures), which is why the capsule tracks we record are delayed neutrons captured on the capsule. Cosmic A–C muons are at the flux rate (~0.6 efficiency per chamber), a tiny share of triggers.

One compact source on the capsule nose, ~10 mm off the frame centre, at every ToF

capsule_pose: ray trace (EAR2 flux × Lambda2D per energy) × Geant4 tracks, +y up · beam off the frame, or capsule off the beam?

capsule_pose early.csv, alternatives.csv, halo.csv, bound.csv

13

Details

Measured. The tracks image one compact source at x -10.4, z ≈ −3.6 mm in the chamber frame, at the nose's height (-31.3 A / -34.6 C). Its x is the same from 2 to 75 ms (the pointing-excess peak, background-robust where the band crossing is not), in every run, and before and after the 27 July access. A and C agree although their u axes point opposite ways, so only a common shift of the pair against the beam could fake it.

What it does not say. The source is where the illuminating neutrons meet Al, not the beam. A compact source at the nose needs a narrow flux on the nose (within ~8 mm, capsule within ±5 mm of its drawn height); grazing lights the 0.6 mm barrel and lifts the source 10–20 mm. A Lambda2D beam centred on the frame reaches x ≈ −10 only with the capsule 13–18 mm off, a flux ×10 wider, or the tail alone, and then puts the source 14–25 mm too high (capsule that much lower than drawn; 1–15 % of the beam on the ³He). The direct-beam window shows no source near x = 0 (≤ 10–34 % at 4–6 ms, ≤ 5 % at 6–12 ms), but the share of direct-beam captures there is unknown: the late, after-the-flux population images the same spot.

Two readings. (1) The flux sits on the capsule, ~10 mm toward B from the frame centre: the beam is not where the frame says, or the frame is not where it was aligned (≥ 85% of the beam then enters the ³He). (2) The beam is centred as aligned and the capsule is far off it and lower than drawn (³He yield 1–15 %). Needs a survey or photo of capsule vs beam, the tip height, and the beam spot at the station. Neither explains the 1 : 8 alone. Report: <out>/capsule_pose/report.html.

Use c1/calib_plastic_e.json for any plastic energy; never the source keVee line above 2 MeV or for the liquids

14

Details

Full write-up: the calorimetry slide note (dylan-neff.web.cern.ch/notes/calorimetry.html) and ntof_calorimetry/PLAN.md "Results so far".

The stack behind each chamber is 3 mm PVT (SiPM wall), 20 mm PVT (plastic) and ~18 mm LAB. It stops an electron of ~5 MeV without the liquid and ~8–9 MeV with it, so for an X17 pair it is a range telescope with dE/dx sampling. The trigger thresholds on the MIP-anchored scale are 2.1–2.9 MeVee, at the ²⁸Al β endpoint, so the planned ²⁸Al calibration (C1.2) is not possible.

In-beam A–C "through-goers" reach the liquid at 0.10 ± 0.04 (A) / 0.04 (C) of the cosmic-muon expectation: they are mostly not penetrating muons.

15

Details

Estimator (mm_charge.py): the sum over the strips on each track's own corridor (from the waveform reco: p0 + depth × tan, depth −3 to 33 mm, ± 5 mm), all 20 samples, pedestal-subtracted. The common mode is taken from each 64-channel block's channels outside the road; the stock CNS would subtract part of a steep track's own charge. An off-road control road averages −0.06 % of the signal. Never the reco's q_sum/q_total (the NNLS runaway).

Chamber C drifts at 28 µm/ns, so its 30 mm gap takes 1.1 µs and its deep charge falls off the 1.2 µs window on ~94 % of tracks. A plateau estimator (charge per sample inside the drift) covers it: σ-equivalent 56 %. The 40 mm gain map spreads 19 % (A) and 39 % (C) cell to cell; the charge is a fine gain monitor.

A first depth profile suggested electron attachment in C (×3 fall with depth). It came from normalising each track on C's minority of in-window tracks; the unbiased all-track profile shows none.

Did the set-up work? Single tracks yes; pairs not yet shown

what the data show

  • Tracking works in the beam: single-track rate within ~20 % of Geant4, a sharp image of the capsule nose at every ToF, angle scale checked on cosmic muons to 1–4 %.
  • The trigger fires on what Geant4 says it should (Compton electrons of the Al γ).
  • Same-chamber correlated pairs exist and their shape is compatible with Al e⁺e⁻.
  • X17 pairs would be the easy topology: two chambers, penetrating legs, self-triggering, vertexing within ~10 mm.

what this does not rule out, and next

  • The pair rate is ⅛ of Geant4 and pair-specific. Until it is understood, the two-track efficiency for close, soft pairs is not demonstrated.
  • The Al pairs cannot be vertexed (scattering), and e⁺e⁻ vs two Compton electrons is not separable without charge or energy.
  • Capsule pose vs beam (~10 mm offset) needs a survey or photo.
  • For LNL: measure the soft leg before ~1 MeV of material; keep the liquid/back layer above its readout threshold; a test pair source with X17-like legs would validate two-track efficiency directly.

16

Details

Next steps for the factor 8 (same-chamber note): re-digitise the Geant4 pairs with is2_v2 (two-sided search, t0 ≤ 300, |tan| < 0.6 on both legs); Geant4 with delayed thermal neutrons on the capsule (the late population); check Geant4's capsule (nose Al thickness, wrap) against the real one; look for a trigger/readout effect specific to two-lepton events.

Why this matters for LNL. The pair deficit could be in the simulation (capsule model, source population) or in the detector (two-track loss in busy events). Only the second would argue against the set-up, and it would hit X17 far less, because X17 legs land in different chambers.
